=== 8229 LANDED AS CHANGE 1132; and 172e HAS A REAL FUNCTIONAL GAP, not a test gap ===

8229 DONE (claimed BEFORE any code this time, per the operator's correction on why the claim gate
exists). Commit c1fc3cee4, Gerrit change 1132.
  runner.py         699 -> 647   (story AC <650 MET; guard <700 met on this patchset)
  structured_run.py 373 -> 477   (guard asserts 100 <= loc < 500; only 23 lines of headroom LEFT --
                                  5e75 targets the SAME module and should plan a second themed
                                  module rather than piling on)
  full suite 8253 passed / 74 skipped / 0 FAILED; lint 0; typecheck 0.

PLAN REVIEW TOOK FOUR ROUNDS AND EVERY ROUND FOUND SOMETHING REAL (findings 1 -> 4 -> 1 -> PASS):
  R1: my own AC ("LOC recorded in the commit message") had NO ORACLE -- a process obligation
      satisfiable by a message written without measuring. Split into a machine-enforced end-state
      (wc -l < 700, which the guard test enforces) plus a GREPPABLE record
      (`runner.py before: <N>` / `runner.py after: <M>`), verifiable with a stated git log command.
  R2: (a) `cache_settings` was MISSING from the planned signature. It is computed at runner.py:381
      as `None if self._model_override else cache_settings_for(caps)` and consumed on the FIRST line
      of the extracted region. An implementer had two exits and one was a REGRESSION: recomputing
      `cache_settings_for(caps)` inside the builder drops the model_override guard and silently
      re-enables cache settings on the offline TestModel path. (b) test_structured_run_seam.py
      hardcodes the moved-symbol lists in TWO places; without updating them the seam guard would
      pass while asserting NOTHING about the new functions.
  R3: `build_usage_limits -> tuple` never named its contents. eff_max_iter is NOT recoverable from
      the UsageLimits it builds -- only max(8, eff_max_iter) is stored as tool_calls_limit and
      max() is not invertible, so for eff_max_iter <= 8 the original is gone. Pinned to
      `tuple[UsageLimits, int, int]` = (usage_limits, req_limit, eff_max_iter).
None of these were cosmetic. All four would have been rework or a live regression had I built first.

HELD-OUT TDD: 14 tests authored, confirmed RED; implementer given ONLY 2 happy-path tests, the other
12 physically removed from its tree. All 14 green on restore. THREE MUTATIONS each caught by a
held-out test: always-send-temperature (withdrawal test), alias cache_settings instead of copying
(8 failures incl. the aliasing test), return req_limit in place of eff_max_iter (the
non-invertibility test). The ordering assertions have teeth.

=== 172e CANNOT CLOSE: the completion verifier found a REAL functional gap. VERIFIED IN SOURCE. ===

I fixed one blocker (the missing through-callers test, change 1128, now Verified +1) and the close
FAILED AGAIN on TWO further criteria. I checked both claims in source before accepting them and the
verifier is RIGHT:

  1. src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml:143-155 -- the `verify` step has NO `model:` key
     at all. It declares prompt / mode / output_schema / with (incl. temperature: 0). So it falls
     through to cfg.model.
  2. src/rebar/llm/config.py:362 -- `resolve_model` is
         return step or workflow or cfg.model
     with NO call to resolve_model_string. So even ADDING `model: standard` to the YAML would pass
     the LITERAL STRING "standard" to the runner rather than resolving the class.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is exactly the split-brain this epic exists to remove: 172e's own title is
"Verifier paths resolve the standard class". It fixed the plan-review path (_verifier_cfg) and the
completion path (completion._verifier_model_for_completion) but NOT the code-review verify step --
which the epic handoff called THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL of the three, since code review is the gate
being cut over to Bedrock. Configure a Bedrock standard class today and code-review's Pass-2 verify
still runs on cfg.model, the FRONTIER DIRECT-ANTHROPIC model. Both of 172e's remaining ACs name this:
"a test asserts code-review's verify step resolves the standard class rather than cfg.model" and
"a test asserts that with classes configured for a non-default provider, no verifier path resolves a
model belonging to a different provider".

REMAINING WORK FOR 172e (in its approved scope, not new scope):
  (a) resolve_model must resolve a class NAME through resolve_model_string;
  (b) code-review.yaml's verify step needs `model: standard`;
  (c) tests for both, including the cross-provider negative control.
NOTE the interaction: 7761 also consumes resolve_model_string for the Pass-1 ladder, and d23e is
blocked by 172e + 7761. Whoever does (a) should check 7761's plan for overlap before implementing.
172e is in_progress with NO assignee -- set one before working it.

=== GERRIT, this firing (the review bot has now voted) ===
  1119 172e      V+1 L+1  submittable=True
  1120 cb6f      V+1 L+1  submittable=True   (ticket CLOSED)
  1121 cc33      V-1 L+1  submittable=True   (Verified SATISFIED by the operator's +1 -- see below)
  1122 ADR 0056  V-1 L+1  submittable=True
  1123 e6bd      V+1 L+1  submittable=True   (ticket CLOSED)
  1128 172e test V+1 L 0  submittable=False  (awaiting LLM-Review only)
  1132 8229      just pushed
CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ENTRY OF MINE: I claimed the CI bot's -1 vetoed 1121/1122 and that the
operator's +1 could not take effect. WRONG. Verified resolves on MAX VALUE, not max-with-block:
/changes/1121?o=SUBMIT_REQUIREMENTS returns "Verified: SATISFIED" even with the bot's -1 still
present, and submittable=True. I had inferred a blocking label from the aggregate LabelInfo instead
of querying the submit requirements. THE SUBMIT REQUIREMENT IS THE AUTHORITY, not the aggregate.

NOT LANDING: rule 4 says land only once the epic closes and every change is green. 1128 still lacks
LLM-Review, and 8229 / a49e / 7761 / d23e / 343b are open.
